python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# Data from December 1941 to December 1942
months = [
    "1941-December",
    "1942-January",
    "1942-February",
    "1942-March",
    "1942-April",
    "1942-May",
    "1942-June",
    "1942-July",
    "1942-August",
    "1942-September",
    "1942-October",
    "1942-November",
    "1942-December"
]

# Bonds (interest-bearing public debt outstanding)
bonds = [40000, 42078, 44305, 44847, 45363, 48157, 48776, 51765, 53680, 54413, 57285, 57931, 64868]

# Bills and certificates of indebtedness (interest-bearing public debt)
bills_ci = [2002, 2101, 2002, 1652, 3460, 3764, 5604, 6759, 8873, 10829, 11336, 12828, 17161]

# Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient
n = len(bonds)
mean_bonds = sum(bonds) / n
mean_bills = sum(bills_ci) / n

# Calculate numerator (covariance)
numerator = sum((bonds[i] - mean_bonds) * (bills_ci[i] - mean_bills) for i in range(n))

# Calculate denominators
sum_sq_bonds = sum((bonds[i] - mean_bonds) ** 2 for i in range(n))
sum_sq_bills = sum((bills_ci[i] - mean_bills) ** 2 for i in range(n))

denominator = math.sqrt(sum_sq_bonds * sum_sq_bills)

pearson_r = numerator / denominator

print(f"Data points: {n}")
print(f"Mean bonds: {mean_bonds}")
print(f"Mean bills: {mean_bills}")
print(f"Sum of squares bonds: {sum_sq_bonds}")
print(f"Sum of squares bills: {sum_sq_bills}")
print(f"Pearson r: {pearson_r}")
print(f"Rounded to 3 decimal places: {round(pearson_r, 3)}")
EOF
